sections.label: Road Traffic Bill aims
sections.summary: The Road Traffic (Miscellaneous Amendments) 2024 Bill seeks to recalibrate deterrence and proportionality for RTA offences and enhance enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Road Traffic (Miscellaneous Amendments) 2024 Bill seeks to: firstly, recalibrate the balance between deterrence and proportionality for RTA offences; and secondly, enhance powers to enforce against errant motorists.

sections.label: Removing minimum sentences first-time offenders
sections.summary: The Bill will remove mandatory minimum sentences and disqualification periods for first-time offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: First, the Bill will remove mandatory minimum sentences and disqualification periods for first-time offenders.

sections.label: Current dangerous driving penalties
sections.summary: Current law requires a minimum one year imprisonment and eight years disqualification for dangerous driving causing grievous hurt.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: If the taxi driver is convicted for dangerous driving causing grievous hurt, the current law requires the Courts to impose a minimum of one year imprisonment and a minimum disqualification from driving of eight years.

sections.label: Court flexibility for contributed accidents
sections.summary: The Court should have flexibility to impose a sentence lower than the statutory minimum where the victim contributed to the accident.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Put simply, in circumstances where the victim had also contributed to the accident, the Court should have the flexibility to impose a sentence lower than the current statutory minimum.

sections.label: Lowering repeat offender minimums
sections.summary: Mandatory minimum imprisonment for repeat offenders will be lowered for dangerous driving causing death and grievous hurt.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: With the removal of the minimum sentences for first-time offenders, we will make corresponding changes to lower the mandatory minimum imprisonment term for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Specifically, for dangerous driving offences causing death for repeat offenders, the mandatory minimum imprisonment term will be lowered from four years to two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For dangerous driving offences causing grievous hurt, it will be lowered from two years to one year.

sections.label: Repeat offender speeding criteria
sections.summary: A motorist is a repeat offender only with at least two prior speeding convictions over 40 km/h, two within five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Specific to a prior conviction of a speeding offence, we will amend the RTA such that a motorist will only be classified and charged as a repeat offender if he satisfies two criteria: first, the motorist had at least two prior speeding convictions in which he had sped in excess of 40 kilometres per hour (km/h) of the road or vehicle's speed limit; and second, at least two of those prior speeding convictions occurred within the five years preceding the motorist's current dangerous or careless driving offence.

sections.label: Speeding charge threshold amendment
sections.summary: This amendment lets authorities focus on recent repeat risk-taking drivers rather than penalising mistakes from over five years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Typically, only those who sped in excess of 40 km/h of the speed limit are charged in Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This amendment allows us to focus on offenders who have exhibited a pattern of risk-taking driving in recent times, without overly penalising offenders for mistakes committed more than five years ago.

sections.label: Disqualification after imprisonment
sections.summary: The Bill makes clear that if an offender is imprisoned, the disqualification period starts from completion of the sentence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Bill will make clear that: if the offender is imprisoned for any offence, the disqualification period will commence from the completion of the sentence.

sections.label: Licence suspension and border breath tests
sections.summary: Clause 4 keeps a motorist's licence suspended until sentencing or disqualification, and Clause 9 lets immigration officers administer border breath tests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill will ensure that the motorist's licence remains suspended, until the final decision is made on the sentencing, or until the disqualification order has commenced, whichever is later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 9 will empower an immigration officer to administer breath tests at the border checkpoints and their vicinity, to detect and take prompt preventive action against errant drink-drivers driving into our checkpoints.

sections.label: Deterrence and proportionality balance
sections.summary: The proposed amendments aim to balance deterrence and proportionality, giving Courts more flexibility in sentencing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments aim to strike a balance between deterrence and proportionality, giving the Courts more flexibility in sentencing.

sections.label: Removing mandatory minimum sentences
sections.summary: Removing mandatory minimum sentences might unintentionally be perceived as leniency even if that is not the intent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are we going soft on offenders?" Removing mandatory minimum sentences might unintentionally be perceived as leniency even if that is not the intent.

sections.label: Foreign vehicles and ICA entry
sections.summary: Clause 2 allows ICA to deny entry or exit for vehicles which have offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How many foreign vehicles have been caught with traffic offences in 2023 or 2024 alone?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 2 allows for ICA to deny entry or exit for vehicles which have offences.

sections.label: Public concern over removed minimum penalties
sections.summary: Members of the public expressed concern about removing mandatory minimum jail terms and disqualification periods for first-time offenders, including reckless or dangerous driving causing death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Members of the public have expressed concern about the removal of the mandatory minimum jail term and mandatory minimum disqualification period for first-time offenders, even in cases of reckless or dangerous driving leading to death.

sections.label: Rising traffic fatalities and speeding accidents
sections.summary: A mid-year report in August 2024 showed traffic fatalities rose 2.8% and fatal speeding accidents nearly doubled from 13 to 25 in the first half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In its mid-year report in August 2024, it was revealed that when comparing the first half of 2024 with the first half of 2023, the number of traffic accident fatalities increased by 2.8% and the number of fatal speeding accidents almost doubled from 13 to 25.

sections.label: PSP opposes removing mandatory penalties
sections.summary: PSP supports other amendments but cannot support removing mandatory minimum sentences and disqualification periods for first-time offenders amid rising fatalities, urging retention for reckless or dangerous driving causing death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We support the other amendments in the Bill, which include, streamlining the commencement dates of disqualification periods and strengthening the Traffic Police's suspension powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, PSP cannot support the amendment to remove mandatory minimum sentence and mandatory minimum disqualification periods for first-time offenders at a time of rising traffic fatalities and fatal speeding accidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We urge the Government to maintain the current mandatory penalties in cases of reckless or dangerous driving leading to death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill being read for the Second time today seeks to remove the mandatory minimum jail term and mandatory minimum disqualification period for first-time offenders who commit dangerous or reckless driving leading to death or grievous hurt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If you compare the first half of 2024 to the first half of 2023, the number of fatalities from traffic accidents increased by 2.8% while fatal speeding accidents nearly doubled from 13 to 25 cases.

sections.label: PSP opposes Bill in current form
sections.summary: PSP opposes the Bill in its current form, saying it removes mandatory minimums for first-time offenders and halves them for repeat offenders, and will support it only if mandatory penalties are retained.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: She also said to make our roads safer we need to strengthen deterrence against irresponsible driving behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, why is the Government now reducing the deterrence effect of this policy at the time when our road safety is in fact deteriorating?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP opposes this amendment. : Madam, we oppose the Bill in its current form, but will support the Bill if amendments are made to retain the current mandatory penalties for reckless or dangerous driving leading to death.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Essentially, today's amendments will remove the mandatory minimum sentence and disqualification period for first-time offenders who are convicted of dangerous or careless driving offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The mandatory minimum sentence for such repeat offenders will be halved.

sections.label: Repeat offender speeding conviction criteria
sections.summary: The Bill proposes a motorist be considered a repeat offender for speeding only with at least two prior speeding convictions exceeding 40 km/h, at least two within the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes that a motorist facing a dangerous or careless driving charge will only be considered a repeat offender vis-a-vis his speeding convictions only if he or she has: one, at least two prior speeding convictions in which the driver sped in excess of 40 km/h of the roads or the vehicle's speed limit; and two, at least two of the prior speeding convictions occurred within the past five years before the motorist's current driving offence.

sections.label: Road traffic deaths in 2023
sections.summary: The SPF's Annual Road Traffic Situation 2023 report states Singapore had about 136 deaths in 2023 due to road traffic accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to the SPF's Annual Road Traffic Situation 2023 report, Singapore suffered about 136 deaths in 2023 due to road traffic accidents.

sections.label: Mandatory sentence for injury driver
sections.summary: The driver who caused the injury faced a mandatory minimum of one year's imprisonment and eight years' disqualification upon conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The driver who caused the injury was, upon conviction, subject to a mandatory minimum of one year's imprisonment and eight years' disqualification.

sections.label: Resident's disqualification reduction question
sections.summary: A first-time offender fined $4,000 and disqualified 60 months asked whether existing disqualification periods can be reduced once the law is passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: One of our residents, a first-time offender with 45 years of unblemished records shared that he was charged for careless driving causing grievous hurt under section 65(1)(b) of the RTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Our resident was fined $4,000 and sentenced under the mandatory disqualification regime to 60 months and still has to serve a remaining period of about 29 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Our resident would like to know whether people like him who were previously sentenced to the mandatory disqualification regime under the existing law will be allowed to have their period of disqualification reduced once the law is passed.

sections.label: Aims of proposed amendments
sections.summary: The proposed amendments aim to recalibrate deterrence and proportionality and to enhance powers to enforce against errant motorists.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments have two primary aims: first, to recalibrate the balance between deterrence and proportionality; and second, to enhance powers to enforce against errant motorists.

sections.label: Rising road casualties and fatalities
sections.summary: While overall road traffic accidents decreased in the first half of 2024, casualties and fatalities rose, with speeding and drink driving fatal accidents rising over three years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, while the number of road traffic accidents overall decreased in the first half of 2024, casualties and fatalities have continued to rise and, concerningly, fatal accidents related to speeding and drink driving have risen over the last three years.

sections.label: Swedish road deaths halved
sections.summary: The initiative led to a halving of deaths on Swedish roads.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The initiative has led to a halving of deaths on Swedish roads.

sections.label: Road safety strategies and foreign workers
sections.summary: Canada and New Zealand are adopting similar road safety strategies, restorative justice is noted for young drivers, and the speaker questions transporting foreign workers in open vehicles without seatbelts while welcoming updates on changes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Countries like Canada and New Zealand are also adopting similar road safety strategies, aiming for zero fatalities and reduced road trauma by 2025 and 2030 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Related is the use of restorative justice procedures to provide meaningful resolutions and support for all parties involved in serious driving offences.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that restorative justice procedures can be particularly useful in resolving those matters involving young drivers who have caused injury or death to a third party as a result of speeding, reckless driving or drug and alcohol misuse, and who show genuine remorse and are prepared to accept responsibility for the consequences of their behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The safety and well-being of foreign workers should be considered no differently to the safety and well-being of other Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I remain puzzled as to why it is still legal to transport multiple foreign workers in open vehicles and without seatbelts, whereas all other drivers and passengers on Singaporean roads are required to wear seatbelts at all times.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that the Government is currently considering changes to these arrangements and I welcome an update on the status and timeline of these changes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we proceed with these amendments, let us commit to regular evaluations of their impact and remain open to further refinements.

sections.label: Removal of mandatory minimum sentences
sections.summary: Concern is raised that removing mandatory minimum sentences and disqualification periods for careless or dangerous driving causing death or grievous hurt does not send a correct deterrence message.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They are concerned about over-penalising motorists who commit traffic infractions which result in relatively less harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, the removal of the mandatory minimum sentences and disqualification periods in the cases of careless or dangerous driving offences causing death or grievous hurt does not seem to be sending the correct message of deterrence.

sections.label: Repeat offender speeding threshold
sections.summary: Clarification is sought on the proposal that a motorist is a repeat offender only if he sped over 40 km/h above the limit at least twice in five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Another amendment that I hope to obtain more clarification on is the proposal for a motorist to be considered as a repeat offender only if he had sped in excess of 40 km/h of the road's speed limit, or the vehicle's speed limit, at least twice within the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Let us consider our demerit points system today, where exceeding the speed limit by more than 40 km/h would cost the motorist 12 demerit points and will be prosecuted in court.

sections.label: Reconsidering the amendment
sections.summary: The Ministry is urged to reconsider the amendment, weighing second chances against deaths and serious injuries from irresponsible motorists' behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While giving second chances is important, we have to weigh against the deaths and serious injuries arising from the behaviour of such irresponsible motorists.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to reconsider this amendment.

sections.label: Recalibrating deterrence and proportionality
sections.summary: After the 2019 amendments were given time to take their course, amendments are now assessed as necessary to recalibrate the balance between deterrence and proportionality.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Following the 2019 amendments, we have given some time for the laws to take their course and we now assess that amendments are necessary to recalibrate the balance between deterrence and proportionality.

sections.label: Courts' flexibility on sentences
sections.summary: The Bill will give the Courts more flexibility to decide appropriate sentences rather than be constrained by statutory minimums.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Bill will give the Courts more flexibility to decide on the appropriate sentences, rather than be constrained by the statutory minimums.

sections.label: Prosecution charging and court discretion
sections.summary: The proposed RTA amendments, including removing mandatory minimums, let the Prosecution proceed with the charge most appropriately reflecting the offence and culpability without impeding the Courts' sentencing discretion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the RTA, including the removal of mandatory minimums, will allow the Prosecution to proceed with the charge that most appropriately reflects the offence committed and the offender's culpability, without impeding the Courts' discretion to mete out an appropriate sentence.

sections.label: Heavier penalties for egregious offenders
sections.summary: The amendment reserves heavier prescribed penalties for recalcitrant and egregious offenders who show deliberate and blatant disregard for road safety.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The proposed amendment reserves the heavier prescribed penalties for recalcitrant and egregious offenders who show a deliberate and blatant disregard for road safety.

sections.label: Penalties apply to future offences
sections.summary: The new set of penalties will only apply to offences committed after the amendments come into force.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The new set of penalties will only apply to offences that are committed after the amendments come into force.

sections.label: Engagement efforts reached 150,000 attendees
sections.summary: In 2024, these engagement efforts reached around 150,000 attendees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2024, these engagement efforts reached around 150,000 attendees.

sections.label: Immigration officers empowered to conduct breath tests
sections.summary: Immigration officers will be empowered to conduct breath tests directly and immediately if they detect any suspected violation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: With the amendment, immigration officers will be empowered to conduct breath tests directly and immediately, should they detect any suspected violation.

sections.label: Foreign vehicles caught for traffic violations
sections.summary: In 2023, about 14,000 foreign vehicles were caught for traffic violations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2023, about 14,000 foreign vehicles were caught for traffic violations.

sections.label: Enforcement against foreign motorists' outstanding fines
sections.summary: Since 2019, foreign vehicles with outstanding fines have been denied entry, and a July 2024 operation stopped 188 foreign motorists to settle fines.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To strengthen enforcement against foreign motorists who violate our laws, since 2019, we have denied foreign vehicles with outstanding fines entry into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In July 2024, the Traffic Police led a multi-agency operation where 188 foreign motorists were stopped and directed to settle their outstanding fines for vehicular and traffic offences when they entered Singapore via the Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: On Mr Yip Hon Weng's concern about seniors who are not digitally savvy, I wish to clarify that summons will only be issued by email if there is prior written consent from the individual.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Police will also put out advisories on how to identify legitimate summonses.

sections.label: Mandatory minimum penalties judicial discretion
sections.summary: The speaker says one mistake can cause a fatal accident, MHA gave no case where the penalty was too harsh, and asks what changed since mandatory minimum penalties began in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: One distraction, one careless mistake, one temptation to speed, is all it takes to cause an accident and lead to a life of regret.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: I asked for an example of actual cases where the accident resulted in death and MHA felt that the penalty was too harsh and the reply was no.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: So, the reason for removing the mandatory minimum penalties was for judicial discretion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Given that the mandatory minimum penalties were introduced in 2019, I would like to ask what has changed.

sections.label: Traffic Police agencies amendment flexibility
sections.summary: From 2019 the Traffic Police and agencies worked together, and the proposed amendment would provide a better option, more flexibility and a fairer sentence regime.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: From 2019 to now, the Traffic Police, as well as the agencies have been working together and also there have been cases whereby, as I shared in my answer, where the current amendment that we are proposing would provide a better option, more flexibility as well as avenues for a fairer sentence regime than what it is available today.
